title: 30005432: property-(s) elements need not form an additive subgroup
original_PR_body:
## Complete counterexample to the original property-(s) ideal question

Constructs an explicit left brace with abelian additive group Z × Z/4. The element x=(0,1) has both defining fixed-subgroup/centralizer indices equal to two, but its additive double (0,2) has an infinite-index right fixed subgroup. Hence the property-(s) elements are not even an additive subgroup. The full property-(s) set, both infinite group laws and failure of two-sidedness are checked directly.

Separate adversarial AI review passed without correction. The proof and source-reconciliation note are unchanged from the reviewed snapshots. All 33,512 submitted assertions replay byte-identically, and 9,562 independent exact controls pass. Nine review files are included.

The audited source-reconciliation note is important: a neighboring 2025 lemma has contextual hypotheses, and its displayed finite-data map cannot be imported unconditionally for arbitrary additive generators. The cited full 2021 finiteness theorem assumes a finite whole star-generated subgroup, which this example does not have. Neither this package nor its review claims that the full 2021 finiteness theorem is false. The review also records the precise finite-quotient diagnostic for the map argument.

Two substantive approach families are recorded (2/5). This is a counterexample to the exact unrestricted original question, without a torsion-free, finite-brace or two-sided claim. Standard construction ingredients are credited; historical priority remains unestablished. AI-reviewed research draft, not human peer reviewed. The coordinating task owns the claimed_solved queue update.
